scorecard.note: Connect the closing to the opening more directly—clearly answer the hook’s question about the cost of pocket change rather than just asking if viewers miss the penny.

storyboard.ears: Pocket change now costs more to make than its face value.
The penny program lost 86 million dollars yearly. Ending production turns that recurring loss into savings.
storyboard.evidence: United States Mint | US penny program: annual loss vs projected savings from ending it | https://www.usmint.gov/about/congressional-reports/annual-report | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: The penny lasted 232 years. Its unusually long production run finally ends under mounting cost pressure.
storyboard.evidence: United States Mint | Years in production before discontinued, selected US coins | https://www.usmint.gov/ | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: A nickel costs 13.78 cents to produce. The next coin problem is already larger than its face value.
storyboard.evidence: United States Mint | Cost to produce one penny vs one nickel, 2024 | https://www.usmint.gov/about/congressional-reports/annual-report | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Ending the penny solves one coin loss while the nickel problem remains.
